review.artifact: Pi Graph Factory local trigger-to-merge controller
review.scope: trusted local or Railway-hosted repositories and configured agent harnesses
review.environment: local macOS/Linux worktrees or a credentialed Railway Cloud Agent; project-configured delivery only
review.assurance_boundary: Safe for trusted-repository trials with merge and delivery disabled by default. Checkpoint recovery, proportional proof, and explicit health-gated delivery are mechanically covered; hostile code, exactly-once external effects, and provider security are not certified.

risks.title: Agent or approved command can use the operator's local permissions
risks.precondition: A request, repository, dependency, or model output is malicious or badly mistaken.
risks.trigger: A configured harness or approved shell command executes locally.
risks.failure: Worktrees isolate Git changes but do not sandbox processes, files, network, or credentials.
risks.effect: Data can be read, changed, or exfiltrated outside the approved repository scope.
risks.evidence: Code inspection: agent_adapter.py launches local harnesses and factory.py runs bash with the invoking environment.
risks.detectability: Repository changes are detected; reads, network calls, and external side effects may not be visible.
risks.recoverability: Git changes can be reverted, but leaked secrets or external effects may be irreversible.
risks.mitigation: Run unfamiliar work in an ephemeral container, VM, or restricted account with minimal credentials and network access.
risks.test: Execute the documented sandbox profile against a canary that attempts out-of-repo write and network access; both must be denied before unattended use.
risks.residual_risk: Kernel, container runtime, provider, and explicitly granted network permissions remain trusted.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Required before running untrusted repositories or unattended production work.

risks.title: Abrupt death can leave ambiguous local or external state
risks.precondition: The controller or host is killed during an agent or repair step.
risks.trigger: SIGKILL, host restart, or provider process loss.
risks.failure: Known Git and process checkpoints can resume, but unknown mutations, background daemons, and external provider effects cannot always be classified.
risks.effect: Ambiguous runs stop for inspection; an external effect may require provider-side reconciliation.
risks.evidence: Deterministic tests cover SIGKILL during an active lane, committed lane/repair reconstruction, declared capture cleanup, partial owner-scoped repair continuation, and recovery after a reviewed fast-forward.
risks.detectability: Inspect exposes the operation, active agents, worktrees, last error, and all durable artifacts; provider state requires provider-side observation.
risks.recoverability: Validated local checkpoints resume. Ambiguous Git mutations and non-idempotent external effects require operator reconciliation.
risks.mitigation: Keep local transitions checkpointed, refuse unknown state, and require idempotent provider commands plus observable health and rollback.
risks.test: Extend death injection across capture and live provider delivery boundaries; assert validated resume locally and explicit reconciliation for ambiguous external effects.
risks.residual_risk: External side effects cannot be made exactly-once by local replay alone.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Required before claiming unattended crash recovery.

risks.title: Schema-valid reviewer can misunderstand visual or product quality
risks.precondition: Tests are incomplete or evidence is ambiguous.
risks.trigger: The independent reviewer returns pass with the current evidence hash.
risks.failure: Evidence provenance is valid but semantic review is wrong.
risks.effect: A functional, design, accessibility, or regression defect reaches merge_ready.
risks.evidence: Controller tests prove provenance and routing, not universal screenshot/video understanding.
risks.detectability: Detected by stronger tests, human review, or post-merge behavior; not guaranteed before authorization.
risks.recoverability: Git rollback is possible if deployment side effects have not occurred.
risks.mitigation: Require target-specific browser/native assertions and a human checkpoint for high-impact releases.
risks.test: Run a visual challenge corpus with known responsive, console, accessibility, and flow defects; measure reviewer misses without changing the corpus.
risks.residual_risk: Novel product defects outside the test and review rubric remain possible.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Human approval remains required for consequential releases.

risks.title: A parallel batch can cross local usage ceilings before all active calls finish
risks.precondition: The approved plan assigns many owners or repair cycles.
risks.trigger: The controller launches up to ten initial agents and repeated reviewers/repairs.
risks.failure: The controller stops later dispatches at configured token and cost ceilings, but cannot preempt already-running parallel lanes and cannot enforce usage a provider does not report.
risks.effect: Unexpected spend, quota exhaustion, or long-running work.
risks.evidence: A deterministic limit test proves the reviewer is not dispatched after implementation usage crosses the ceiling; schema and code inspection show the initial approved lanes launch concurrently.
risks.detectability: Usage receipts expose reported spend after calls; null provider usage weakens visibility.
risks.recoverability: Future dispatch can stop, but completed provider spend cannot be recovered.
risks.mitigation: Use conservative local ceilings with require_usage where supported, plus provider-side account budgets for hard spend control.
risks.test: Use fixture usage that crosses each ceiling and assert later agents are not dispatched while active work drains visibly.
risks.residual_risk: Already-running parallel calls can overshoot and provider-reported usage can lag or be absent, so local ceilings are dispatch controls rather than hard spend guarantees.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Required before large or unattended swarms.

risks.title: The plan-quality judge can over-score or under-score a valid plan
risks.precondition: A generated plan contains domain nuance not represented well by the anchored rubric or model.
risks.trigger: The independent plan judge scores a candidate plan.
risks.failure: A weak plan clears 8.5 or a strong plan repeatedly fails the threshold.
risks.effect: Bad implementation scope can reach human approval, or useful work stops after three cycles.
risks.evidence: Deterministic tests validate scoring arithmetic and revision control flow, but no large human-rated calibration corpus exists yet.
risks.detectability: Every candidate, dimension score, evidence statement, improvement, and final judgment is durable for inspection.
risks.recoverability: The operator can refuse approval, revise the request, or provide a trusted external plan.
risks.mitigation: Build a frozen human-rated corpus from step-by-step factory runs and calibrate anchors, threshold, and disagreement handling before unattended production claims.
risks.test: Score the same hidden plan corpus with humans and the judge; measure false passes, false failures, stability, and actionable revision gain.
risks.residual_risk: Novel repositories and product decisions can remain outside the calibration distribution.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Calibration required before removing exact operator plan approval.

risks.title: Repository intelligence executes a parser and may call a semantic provider
risks.precondition: Graphify, a parser dependency, or the configured semantic endpoint is compromised, unapproved, or behaves unsafely on adversarial source.
risks.trigger: The controller auto-installs or executes Graphify before planning or merge; semantic enrichment is enabled when supported repository documents exist.
risks.failure: The external package runs with the invoking account's permissions and reads the target repository; supported docs, papers, and images are sent to the configured semantic provider by design.
risks.effect: Repository contents or local credentials could be exposed or changed outside factory Git controls, or sensitive documentation could leave the trusted environment.
risks.evidence: Code inspection and a live test show pinned uv auto-install, local AST extraction, and optional DeepSeek-compatible semantic extraction; worktrees are not OS sandboxes.
risks.detectability: Generated repository changes are visible to Git checks; reads and network effects may not be visible.
risks.recoverability: Git-local output is disposable, but leaked data or external effects may be irreversible.
risks.mitigation: Preinstall and audit Graphify in a restricted runner, disable auto-install or semantic enrichment for sensitive repositories, approve the configured data processor, and isolate untrusted repositories from valuable credentials.
risks.test: Run the pinned package in the documented restricted runner against parser fuzz fixtures and assert no out-of-repository writes or unexpected network access.
risks.residual_risk: The Python runtime, parser binaries, package index, and runner remain trusted dependencies.
risks.acceptance_review_condition: Required before hostile-repository or unattended-production claims.
